tests.title: Tests are not a luxury
tests.text: The product went down, and you remembered it.

buyers.title: I know procurement
buyers.text: You survived the procurement department and its requirements spreadsheet.
buyers.gives: 20 enterprise prospects in the starting funnel; their requirements still need to be met

word.title: I keep my word
word.text: You promised clients what didn’t exist — and managed to build it. Twice.
word.gives: a promised block gets three sprints instead of two

no.title: Learned to say “no”
no.text: A broken promise cost more than an honest answer.
no.gives: an honest answer on a call costs a 15% discount instead of 25%

banker.title: I know my banker
banker.text: You mortgaged the flat and bought it back. The bank remembered.
banker.gives: the mortgage buys 75 seconds instead of 50

arch.title: I see the architecture
arch.text: Three combos in one product is no longer an accident.
arch.gives: each friendly connection adds 16% to bills instead of 8%

name.title: A name on the market
name.text: Ten clients in one startup: people started to recognize you.
name.gives: the first client of the next startup is a chain right away

ear.title: I know how to listen
ear.text: Turns out you can just ask the clients.
ear.gives: 15 small-business prospects in the starting funnel

cash.title: An exit on the résumé
cash.text: You sold a company and now put it in every bio.

cheapEarly.title: I know the price of tokens
cheapEarly.text: You turned a profit and understood what exactly did it.
cheapEarly.gives: the “Cheaper Model” block is available from the first sprint

posts.title: A post about failure
posts.text: Your post “Shutting down my startup: ten lessons” got more attention than the startup itself.
posts.gives: the first client is already waiting: one lead at the start

template.title: My own template
template.text: You can now put together a Claude wrapper with your eyes closed.
template.gives: the product core is already in place at the start
